title: Geothermal and volcanic areas in New Zealand and Italy did not repeat the US 3 h response to distant M6.5+ waves (2005-2026); only Kythira 2006 at Etna and Kaikoura 2016 in the TVZ gave clear cases
abstract: A campaign study found that distant M6.5+ earthquakes raised 3 h catalogue rates in US geothermal and volcanic areas by 2.14 times at an estimated peak dynamic stress of 1 kPa or more and 4.11 times at 3 kPa or more, but not in tectonic areas. We tested this result in two independent networks with the same code. We set 18 regions before the download: 10 geothermal fields and volcanoes and 8 tectonic controls in New Zealand (GeoNet, 2012-2026) and Italy (INGV, 2005-2026), depth 20 km or less, with magnitude cuts from completeness. The triggers were the same ComCat M6.5+ list at 400 km or more. Placebo origins shifted by 5-120 days gave the null. In the primary clean-window test, the pooled geothermal and volcanic regions had 3 events in the 3 h window where 6.1 were expected at 1 kPa or more (factor 0.51, one-sided 95% upper limit 1.45) and 2 where 2.2 were expected at 3 kPa or more (upper limit 2.9). The US factors are outside these limits (p = 0.002 and 0.006), and New Zealand and Italy each excluded the US factor at 1 kPa or more. Tectonic controls were flat. With the secondary dominant-window rule the geothermal factor was 5.0 at 3 kPa or more, but two triggers carried it: the 2006 Kythira M6.7 earthquake, after which a 19-event Etna swarm started 1.75 h after the waves, and the 2016 Kaikoura M7.8 earthquake (about 130 kPa) in the Taupo Volcanic Zone. Without them the factor was 0.42 at 1 kPa or more (upper limit 1.25). A Kawerau swarm started 37.5 h after a 2023 Kermadec M7.0, but an exploratory test of 73 burst onsets found no clear excess within 5 days of strong waves (4 against 2.5 expected). Thus remote triggering in these areas occurred in single cases, not as a general US-size response. Limitations: small expected counts (factors below 1.45 cannot be excluded), approximate stress values, national catalogue cuts, and post hoc case and burst analyses.

display.caption: 3 h response factor (observed rate divided by expected rate) for geothermal/volcanic and tectonic regions in New Zealand, Italy and both, with one-sided 95% limits, for distant M6.5+ triggers at 1 kPa or more and 3 kPa or more. The shaded top row is the US result under test. The primary clean-rule results exclude the US factor; the dominant-rule excess goes away when Kythira 2006 and Kaikoura 2016 are left out.

Cumulative catalogue events around the surface-wave start for the three single cases: Etna after the 2006 Kythira M6.7 earthquake (swarm from 1.75 h), the Taupo Volcanic Zone after the 2016 Kaikoura M7.8 earthquake, and Kawerau after the 2023 Kermadec M7.0 earthquake (swarm from 37.5 h).

Superposed-epoch rates relative to the 10-day background for pairs at 3 kPa or more, clean rule (top) and dominant rule (bottom), with 95% placebo ranges. Only the dominant rule gives a 1-3 h geothermal excess, mostly from the Etna swarm; the 24-48 h bin is the Kawerau swarm.
